examples.purpose: Claim an expense, the guide's In context: the field sits in a Card above Submit claim. Shown after people tapped Submit claim with no receipt, so the screen has set isInvalid and the message, and the button stays enabled. The empty attachments list, the onAttachmentsChange stub and the picker stub stand in for the app's own list of files and its own picker.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <VStack>
    <FormUpload
      label="Receipts"
      maxCount={3}
      supportText="Up to 3 photos, JPG or PNG"
      attachments={[]}
      onAttachmentsChange={() => {}}
      picker={async () => ({ assets: [] })}
      isInvalid
      errorMessage="Add at least one receipt"
    />
    <Button label="Submit claim" onPress={() => {}} />
  </VStack>
</Card>

from.quote: When people tap Submit without a receipt, the screen sets the error; the button stays enabled.

examples.purpose: Two receipts with a limit of three: each file shows as a preview with a remove button named after it (Remove Receipt 1), the add cell follows, and the support text gives the file rules. The uris are placeholders for the app's files, and the picker stub stands in for the app's picker.
examples.jsx:
<FormUpload
  label="Receipts"
  maxCount={3}
  supportText="JPG or PNG, up to 5 MB each"
  attachments={[
    { uri: 'https://example.com/receipt-1.jpg', name: 'Receipt 1' },
    { uri: 'https://example.com/receipt-2.jpg', name: 'Receipt 2' },
  ]}
  onAttachmentsChange={() => {}}
  picker={async () => ({ assets: [] })}
/>

from.quote: Each file shows as a preview with a remove button, an add cell follows, and support text sits below.

examples.purpose: At the limit: three receipts with maxCount 3, so the add cell is hidden and people can tell they're done; removing one brings it back. The uris are placeholders for the app's files, and the picker stub stands in for the app's picker.

props.name: label
props.description: On the web it names the field, a group, and the add button, such as “Receipts, add attachment”. Declared: Label rendered above the upload row.

props.name: supportText
props.description: Helper text rendered below the upload row. When `errorMessage` is provided, it replaces the support text and renders in the error status.

props.name: name
props.description: Field name. When used inside `<Form>`, this is the key used to look up server-side `validationErrors`.

props.name: attachments
props.description: Each attachment renders a preview cell (testID-item-N) that shows its uri as an image (cover), with a remove control; there is no file icon or name, so a non-image file has no thumbnail. File type and size are not checked. Declared: Controlled list of attachments. Each item maps to an `Additem` cell: render attachments as `'preview'` cells and leave the last slot as the `'empty'` upload trigger.

props.name: maxCount
props.description: One empty add cell (testID-add) follows the previews while attachments.length < maxCount, or always when maxCount is unset. Picked assets beyond maxCount are dropped. Declared: Maximum number of attachments allowed. When omitted, the component renders a single empty upload trigger. Once `attachments.length` reaches `maxCount`, the empty trigger is hidden.

props.name: onAttachmentsChange
props.description: Called when the attachment list should change (add or remove). The parent is responsible for updating the `attachments` array.

props.name: picker
props.description: Optional picker injected by the parent. This keeps the component free of native-library dependencies while still providing real upload behaviour on iOS/Android. The picker should wrap `react-native-image-picker`, `expo-image-picker`, `react-native-document-picker`, etc.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Replaces supportText only while isInvalid (or a Form error) is set. Invalid changes nothing else: the cells keep their colours. Declared: Error message shown below the row. When provided inside `<Form>`, the form context error is used automatically unless this prop is set explicitly.

props.name: isInvalid
props.description: The support text turns red (rgb(245, 0, 48)) with a warning icon; the cells are unchanged. Declared: Marks the field as invalid. Also set automatically by `<Form>` errors. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Each cell renders at 0.5 opacity once, with the label at full opacity; adding and removing are blocked, and the cells leave the tab order. Declared: Disables all upload interaction. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom children/slot rendered in place of the generated `Additem` cells. Useful when the consumer wants full control over the upload row. `modes` cascade into slot children automatically.

props.name: style
props.description: Style overrides for the outermost wrapper.

props.name: rowStyle
props.description: Style overrides for the upload row container.

props.name: testID
props.description: Each preview gets testID-item-N, a wrapper holding the preview button and its remove button as siblings, and the add cell gets testID-add. Declared: Test identifier.

gaps.text: Previews show images only: there is no file icon or name, so a non-image file, such as a PDF, has no thumbnail.
Figma has no error or disabled design: in the package an error only changes the support text, and disabled fades the cells to half opacity.
Figma's FormUpload puts its Add Item cells in one clipped row; the package wraps the row and always puts the add cell last.
Cells are 44 × 44 px in the package and 45 × 44 in Figma.
